new.title: Stroll Place Plumereau in Vieux-Tours
new.desc: The heart of Vieux-Tours is ringed by half-timbered and stone houses dating from the 12th to 16th centuries, many protected as historic monuments. The square was once the place aux Fruits and took the name of Charles Plumereau in 1888; the old quarter was restored in the 1960s.
new.tip: Come in the morning for the architecture before the terraces fill up. Adjacent lanes such as rue du Grand Marché reward a wander.
new.q: Place Plumereau, Vieux Tours, Tours

new.title: Admire the Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Gatien
new.desc: Built between about 1170 and 1547 after a fire destroyed the Romanesque church, it shows the full span of Gothic style from the 13th-century choir to the flamboyant façade, with Renaissance lanterns crowning the towers. Inside are the tomb of the children of Anne of Brittany and Charles VIII and a great organ given in 1522.
new.tip: Free to enter, but it is an active place of worship so check visiting hours. Walk round to the north side for the best view of the flying buttresses.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Gatien, Place de la Cathédrale, Tours

new.title: Climb the spiral stair of the Cloître de la Psalette
new.desc: This cloister beside Saint-Gatien cathedral blends flamboyant Gothic and Renaissance galleries and is run by the Centre des monuments nationaux. Its north-east spiral staircase recalls the one in the François I wing of the château de Blois and leads to the scriptorium; Balzac set a scene of his Comédie humaine here.
new.tip: Enter via the cathedral's north aisle; a small fee applies. The upper terrace gives a close view of the gargoyles.
new.q: Cloître de la Psalette, Rue de la Psalette, Tours

new.title: Visit the Beaux-Arts museum and its giant cedar
new.desc: The Musée des Beaux-Arts occupies the former archbishops' palace beside the cathedral. Its French-style garden holds a huge protected cedar of Lebanon and, under glass, the stuffed elephant Fritz, who came from a circus.
new.tip: The garden and the cedar are free to see. Allow an hour or two inside for the paintings.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts, 18 Place François Sicard, Tours

new.title: Visit the Basilique Saint-Martin and Tour Charlemagne
new.desc: The neo-Byzantine basilica rebuilt after the tomb of Saint Martin was rediscovered in 1860 has a crypt with the saint's tomb. The nearby Tour Charlemagne and Tour de l'Horloge are medieval remains of the earlier abbey church.
new.tip: Free entry; the two towers stand a few minutes away on rue des Halles. Guided visits are listed on the basilica's website.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Martin, Rue Descartes, Tours

new.title: Discover the Château de Tours and its Logis des Gouverneurs
new.desc: The riverside château, whose Logis des Gouverneurs dates from the 16th century and overlaps the old Gallo-Roman wall, now serves as an exhibition venue for photography, contemporary art and heritage displays. A permanent exhibition retraces the history of Tours.
new.tip: Check the programme on the city's site since exhibitions change. It sits near the Loire quays, about ten minutes' walk from Place Plumereau.
new.q: Château de Tours, 25 Avenue André Malraux, Tours

new.title: See masterpieces at the Musée du Compagnonnage
new.desc: Housed in the former monks' dormitory of the Benedictine Saint-Julien abbey, this museum holds masterworks, tools and archives of the Compagnons du Tour de France. It opened in 1968 and is a Musée de France.
new.tip: Enter through the abbey courtyard from rue Nationale; check the official site for hours.
new.q: Musée du Compagnonnage, 8 Rue Nationale, Tours

new.title: Wander the Jardin botanique de Tours
new.desc: The municipal botanical garden and arboretum covers about five hectares and is the city's oldest garden, created between 1831 and 1843. It has heath, bog, Mediterranean and alpine areas, an orangery and exhibition greenhouses.
new.tip: Free and open daily; the Biodivers greenhouses open 14h to 17h and close from 15 November to 1 February.
new.q: Jardin botanique, 35 Boulevard Tonnellé, Tours

new.title: Walk across the Pont Wilson over the Loire
new.desc: Built between 1765 and 1778, the 15-arch, 434 m stone bridge was first called the Pont Royal and was renamed in 1918 after Woodrow Wilson. A section collapsed in April 1978 and the bridge was rebuilt.
new.tip: The quays on both banks give the best views, especially at sunset.
new.q: Pont Wilson, Tours

new.title: Visit the Prieuré Saint-Cosme, Ronsard's home
new.desc: On the Loire at La Riche, this priory was home for twenty years to the poet Pierre de Ronsard. The visit takes in the refectory restored after the 1944 bombing, the garden of medicinal plants and the prior's lodging.
new.tip: Free parking on site; opening days are mainly Thursday to Sunday, so check prieure-ronsard.fr. Fil Bleu bus line 15 stops nearby.
new.q: Prieuré Saint-Cosme, Rue Ronsard, La Riche

new.title: See the Château du Plessis-lès-Tours where Louis XI died
new.desc: Louis XI made this his main residence after acquiring the estate in the 1460s and died here on 30 August 1483. Only one wing with a stair tower survives; it has been a listed monument since 1927 and now hosts a cultural project and a park.
new.tip: Check opening and events with La Riche before going since the site changed hands in 2025.
new.q: Château du Plessis-lès-Tours, La Riche

new.title: Look over the Loire from La Lanterne de Rochecorbon
new.desc: This tower, the only surviving piece of the former castle of Rochecorbon, stands above limestone cliffs on the Loire and is a protected monument. It served as a landmark for boatmen and is a viewpoint on hiking and cycling routes.
new.tip: Check access and hours on the Rochecorbon town hall site. Reachable by a loop walk from Tours or from Rochecorbon village.
new.q: Tour dite La Lanterne, Rochecorbon

new.title: Graze the stalls of Les Halles de Tours
new.desc: The covered market on Place Gaston-Pailhou was begun in 1864 to a design by Gustave Guérin inspired by the halles of Paris. Butchers, fishmongers and charcutiers sell rillettes de Tours and other Touraine produce.
new.tip: Go in the morning for the best choice, then eat at a counter or take picnic food to the Loire quays.
new.q: Les Halles de Tours, Place Gaston Pailhou, Tours

new.title: Taste rillettes de Tours at Maison Hardouin
new.desc: Hardouin is a Vouvray charcuterie with a counter in the Halles de Tours, known for rillettes de Tours, rillons and andouillette. Rillettes de Tours have IGP status.
new.tip: Buy a jar of rillettes and a few rillons for a picnic; also sold at its shop in Vouvray.
new.q: Maison Hardouin, Les Halles, Place Gaston Pailhou, Tours

new.title: Dine at Les Bartavelles on rue Colbert
new.desc: A small modern-French restaurant at 33 rue Colbert run by a pair of young siblings, with a Marcel Pagnol theme per the Michelin Guide, which lists it with a €€€ price tier.
new.tip: Book ahead; the dining room is small.
new.q: Les Bartavelles, 33 Rue Colbert, Tours

new.title: Book a table at La Rissole, Place du Grand Marché
new.desc: A small bistronomic restaurant run by Guillaume and Laetitia Dallay at 51 place du Grand Marché, with a short seasonal menu built on regional produce. It is in the Michelin Guide at €€.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday for lunch and dinner; there are only a few tables, so reserve.
new.q: La Rissole, 51 Place du Grand Marché, Tours

new.title: Buy nougat de Tours at Pâtisserie Nicolas Léger
new.desc: Gault&Millau describes Nicolas Léger as the go-to pastry chef of Tours, with pâtisserie, chocolates and ice cream at 59 place du Grand-Marché. Reviewers single out the nougat de Tours.
new.tip: Closed Mondays according to listings. Check hours before you go.
new.q: Pâtisserie Nicolas Léger, 59 Place du Grand Marché, Tours

new.title: Have a drink at Le Vieux Mûrier on Place Plumereau
new.desc: A student-friendly institution at 11 place Plumereau with a large terrace on the square. It is known for a house white beer flavoured with blackberry and a signature burger.
new.tip: Open late most days; Sunday hours are shorter.
new.q: Le Vieux Mûrier, 11 Place Plumereau, Tours

new.title: Sip Loire wines at Le Bistrot des Belles Caves
new.desc: A wine bar and bistro at 23 rue du Commerce between rue Nationale and Place Plumereau. Tastings come with tapas or boards, and there is a patio at the back.
new.tip: Reserve for dinner; opening days vary, so check ahead.
new.q: Le Bistrot des Belles Caves, 23 Rue du Commerce, Tours

new.title: Order a draft beer at Au Temps des Rois
new.desc: A bar and bistro on the corner of Place Plumereau, with over a dozen draught beers, cocktails and local wines. Its main draw is the sunny terrace.
new.tip: Open from morning until late, with sharing boards available all day.
new.q: Au Temps des Rois, 3 Place Plumereau, Tours

new.title: Dine at Les Hautes Roches in the Rochecorbon cliff
new.desc: A hotel-restaurant at 86 quai de la Loire in Rochecorbon, in an 18th-century manor built into the tufa cliff, with terraces facing the Loire. It is in the Michelin Guide (€€€) and rated 13/20 by Gault&Millau.
new.tip: Reserve ahead, especially for a terrace table in summer.
new.q: Les Hautes Roches, 86 Quai de la Loire, Rochecorbon

new.title: Savour a seasonal soufflé at La Roche Le Roy
new.desc: A restaurant in an 18th-century manor at 55 route de Saint-Avertin, south of the centre, with chef Maximilien Bridier and modern French cooking. Frommer's highlights its seasonal soufflé, and the Michelin Guide lists it at €€€.
new.tip: A short drive or bus ride from the centre; book ahead.
new.q: La Roche Le Roy, 55 Route de Saint-Avertin, Tours

new.title: Taste sparkling Vouvray in the Marc Brédif cellars
new.desc: Maison Marc Brédif, founded in 1893 at 87 quai de la Loire in Rochecorbon, has large troglodytic cellars hollowed from the tufa and is known for sparkling Vouvray. Guided visits end in a tasting.
new.tip: Book in advance through the winery or booking platforms; offers range from a roughly 60-minute visit to a 90-minute guided tour.
new.q: Maison Marc Brédif, 87 Quai de la Loire, Rochecorbon

new.title: Tour the Cave de Vouvray cooperative cellars
new.desc: A cooperative founded in 1953 that brings together about 35 growers on some 450 ha of vines, with troglodytic caves that visitors can tour with a tasting. Vintage sparkling wines and sweet moelleux wines are the highlights.
new.tip: Tastings and visits are offered on booking platforms; confirm price and times first.
new.q: Cave de Vouvray, 38 Rue de la Vallée Coquette, Vouvray

new.title: Spend an evening at the Tours sur Loire guinguette
new.desc: A summer open-air café at the foot of the Pont Wilson on the Loire banks, with a restaurant serving local dishes and regular music. It is open roughly from May to late September.
new.tip: Reserve if you want to eat; the dates are 2 May to 27 September per the listing.
new.q: Guinguette de Tours sur Loire, 1 Quai de la Loire, Tours

new.title: Cycle the Loire à Vélo from Tours towards Villandry
new.desc: The Tours to Villandry stage follows the south bank of the Cher, with a voie verte beginning at the Piscine du Lac and passing Savonnières on the way.
new.tip: Parkings are at Tours Piscine du Lac, Savonnières and Villandry; stage details on francevelotourisme.com.
new.q: Piscine du Lac, Tours

new.title: Hike the vineyards above Rochecorbon
new.desc: Marked loops start in Rochecorbon and cross the Vouvray vineyards past tufa houses and troglodyte cellars, with a roughly 184 m climb on one reviewed circuit of about 2h40.
new.tip: Routes are on Visorando and Decathlon Outdoor; start from the village centre and wear boots after rain.
new.q: Rochecorbon village centre, Rochecorbon

new.title: Browse the Boulevard Béranger flower market and brocante
new.desc: Under the plane trees of Boulevard Béranger there is a flower market on Wednesday and Saturday mornings, and a professional brocante on the fourth Sunday of each month.
new.tip: Brocante typically 7am to 7pm and free; confirm dates with the city of Tours.
new.q: Boulevard Béranger, Tours

new.title: Join the guided Vieux Tours walk
new.desc: A 1h30 guided walk of the Vieux Tours quarter around Place Plumereau, run by the city's heritage service under the Ville d'Art et d'Histoire label.
new.tip: Costs from 7 euros, in French; book through the Tours tourist office and arrive 10 minutes early.
new.q: Office de Tourisme Tours Val de Loire, Rue Bernard Palissy, Tours

new.title: Catch a gig at the Aucard de Tours festival
new.desc: A rock and alternative festival launched by Radio Béton in 1986. It runs five evenings in early June under two tents on the Plaine de la Gloriette.
new.tip: Fil Bleu tram stops at L'Heure Tranquille; check aucard-tours.com for dates since the 2027 lineup was not confirmed.
new.q: Plaine de la Gloriette, 33 Route de Savonnières, Tours
